[b] January 2, 2027: Rumblings[/b]

As the First Council convened once more following the holiday celebrations and a victorious new years celebration led by Piter Drømm, three things appeared on their radar.

Firstly, with the declaration of the Republic of Knygta and Deyn, the right to peoples self determination had been firmly established by the silence of the council, already the former seat of the doge on the council had been vacated and was awaiting its swift filling by the handpicked PRA commander Alexander Ptoljns. However the SCSI reported that while Knygta and Deyn, and Gossen had been peacefully declared, rumblings had appeared in Angmaar against the Prince there who had been a consistent opponent to the local council that had been set up there with the help of the CPNTs national cadre, refusing to even attend the meetings of that council or grant assent to their demands. It was thus decided to censure the prince of Angmaar for his actions, which in the words of Malben, Threatened the stability of Thýven,.

Secondly, the Ministry of Finance under Lenstahl, had presented to the council a grave report stating that due to the massive political and economic shifts that Thýven had undergone the GDP had contracted in 2026 by 2-3% and was on track to lose another 2% in the coming quarter. The report called for a restructuring of the economy and vast prevention measures and programs across the federal states to prevent the further slowdown of the economy. The council however would defer a vote on any measures until January 7 when the Second Peoples Congress was to be called by Malben

Thirdly, Piter Drømm, despite being deposed in December, it was without a doubt that he held a special place in the overall hearts of the people, having helped topple a destabilizing force in the country. Thus under the direction of the council, the position of President of the Union would be created, a purely ceremonial and diplomatic position acting as the head of government but with nominal powers and subsequently reporting to the Chairman of the First Council. This move would be to further centralise the offices of the First Council under the Revolutionary Mandate.

[spoiler=[b]Operation Red Falcon: Phase 4[/b]]
With all major exits to Vald now blocked by either Hydronian or Valdderan forces, it was now time to execute the most crucial part of Operation Red Falcon; The capture of Vald. It was this offensive that would decide whether the operation would succeed or fail, and it was this offensive that could make it break a new future for Valdderans, free from ISV-imposed tyranny.

The attack would begin during the night. Evacuation orders had been issued to all civilians residing within Vald and the surrounding areas to avoid any accusations of war crimes. The armoured vehicles and artillery on the ground would go first, supported by HH-194Y fighters, known to the soldiers as Yatlikart, in the air. Whilst the Yatlikarts carried out air-to-surface strikes on any potential enemy defences surrounding Vald, the artillery would pummel the edge of the citys taking out vital enemy positions in preparation for a storm of the city.

Once enemy positions had been taken out, the storm would hit. Armoured vehicles would roll into the urban streets of Vald. Tanks would fire shells across entire roads at enemy positions on the other side. Behind the tanks and armoured vehicles, the foot soldiers would rush in. They would take up sniper and machine gunner positions in high-rise apartments, and take cover behind abandoned buildings, engaging in rifle gunfights with the opposition. The superior skill of Hydronias well trained army would likely result in a victory, bringing Vald under Hydronian control. President Bozkan would be very aware that a Daesunite invasion was imminent, so, unlike the other captured cities, he would order that they remain under Hydronian military control to deter the eastern giant from planting its flag on mainland Valddera.

In the eastern parts of the country, the zone 2 offensive would be making slow, but steady progress. However, this was not enough. Hydronian forces would decide to take a different strategy, capturing first the northwestern highway to Green Town. From Green Town, the army could use transport links to fan out and attack from behind enemy lines. As always, close air support would help massively.

The search for the leader of the ISV, now codenamed h by Hydronias cobra team, would continue. Each day the team would get closer and closer to finding hs position. This would be helped by a newer search strategy, which involved flying the stealth helicopters lower, but having 5th Gen HH-206 fighters escort the helicopters. The helicopters would also be fitted with several EW devices for radio interception, as well as the existing thermal imaging. These measures would bring cobra team to carry out the most intensive search for an individual in Hydronias history.

With the White Sea crisis over, Hydronia would divert its small naval force in the Bobian commonwealth towards the shamat sea. Coupled with the already present forces left over from the blockade incident, and ships that would be further deployed from ports and bases in Turqevia, Hydronia would spread its presence across the entire shamat sea. The ships would be careful not to enter Daesunite or Blobon territorial waters in an attempt to avoid any international controversy. The alias of this fleet would be a peacekeeping operation. This would hold true, but these ships would also quietly observe naval Daesuns operations, making use of radar, but also satellite imagery from above.

In addition to the naval fleet, several squadrons of E-sahin-55 fighters would be deployed into the air above the shamat sea and Hydronian occupied airspace in Valddera. These fighters, specifically designed for air superiority, would do what it says on the tin; maintain Hydronian air superiority. This would work to dissuade a Daesunite attack on Hydronian ships and Hydronian-held territory, whilst also acting as show of power for Hydronias airforce and navy, which had taken heavy hits in the THEP-EDU war, but since recovered and improved thanks to careful spending plans.
[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Statement to Daesun and the international community[/b]]
[i]Hydronia has refused Daesunite demands to pull out of Valddera ahead of Daesuns attacks. Daesun retains no right to interfere in Valdderas affairs and any invasion will be considered as a threat to Valdderan stability and counterterror operations. This attempt to shove Hydronia out of the way is seen as a deliberate hindrance to the fight against the ISV, who Hydronia is actively working to destroy. Hydronia reaffirms that its some objective in Valddera is the destruction of the ISV and other terror groups, remaining neutral in the governmental affairs of Valddera. Additionally, a clear warning is given to Daesun, that any attacks on Hydronian-held territory will be considered an act of hostility.

Whilst Hydronia will not pull military forces out of Valddera, in the spirit of continuing Hydro-Daesunite cooperation, civil evacuation orders have been given to the local island districts of Samzad and Izib. Despite this, Hydronia would warn Daesun that if any harm comes to Hydronian citizens or interests, it could mean war.[/i]
[/spoiler]

[b] January 3-4, 2027: The Protests of Angmaar and the Bloody Night[/b]

The Prince of Angmaar had called a speech for the principate, ordering the Principates own levy to gather the loyalists to the great square of the city of Rysse, the home of the former royal house of Rysse. Thus, almost seven hundred loyalists filled the square, with the prince coming out to give a speech. But something was wrong when he stepped out from the dark interior of the palace, the masses were far larger than what he had expected, protest banners filled the square as chants of Down with the tyrant! and Freedom to the council! filled the air. On the sidelines, SCSI officers quietly stood in civilian clothes observing the crowd. 

Angmaar began to speak, he spoke about freedom, about the glory of the old monarchy, and he made promises to ensure the stability of the council of Angmaar, however, the crowd soon grew loud enough to drown out the speech.

Guards stationed at the base of the balcony near the entrance to the palace jostled and tried to push back the now surging crowd, who refused to be placated by the pleas of the prince.

As the chaos and noise rose, the private security of the prince would inform him that the rear of the palace had been breached by protestors, forcing the prince to depart from the balcony in haste. A brief scuffle occurred within the palace as protestors confronted the guards and private security, shots would be fired, killing two guards, with the return fire killing a protester. As the sounds of shots echoed through the building, the crowd surged forward, overwhelming the guard cordone, and swarming the entrance of the building, with protestors breaking basement windows to get into the building.

In the meantime the prince and the remaining security rushed to the roof of the palace where an SCSI helicopter was waiting, having arrived an hour later due to an order from the First Council to Ensure the safety of the prince,. 

However, access to the helicopter soon was blocked off by protestors who had taken a rear servant's staircase to the roof. After a brief fire-fight between SCSI agents near the helicopter (with shots damaging the helicopter rotors), the protestors overwhelmed the guards of the prince, dragging the prince himself to the ground in fury. 

What happened next would later be heavily debated by the emergency SCSI tribunal, with conflicting reports that a knife was drawn and stabbed into the princes body, another that the prince was shot at point blank range during the struggle. Autopsy reports later released would show the prince had been initially stabbed twenty times before an accidental discharge of a protestors pistol would puncture his lung, killing him instantly. 

As further SCSI re-enforcements arrived on the roof to disperse the protestors, it became clear that the prince had been killed, though the beating and stabbings had made the body near unrecognisable. 

Following this, several warning shots were fired from the ground SCSI agents, forcing the crowd into a panic, a stampede would follow with almost two hundred individuals being trampled in the square, as further SCSI agents moved to reorganise the palace guard and push the crowd out of the square.

Videos of the incidents in Rysse by this time filled Thývenic news media and social media as the First Council convened in an emergency meeting, consisting only of three members, the prince of Gossen,  the chairman of The Republic of Knygta and Deyn Alexander Ptoljns, and Chairman Malben himself. A quick vote would be taken to bring out a contingent of NDF troops from the local garrison to the city of Rysse, numbering around 2,000 along with 12 V-90 ACVs from the neighboring principate of Tharkønn. Following this vote, another vote was taken to summon the Council of Angmaar to hold a special session (at this time the council had already convened in order to coordinate the take-over of the government of Angmaar, unbeknownst to the First Council at the time). 

As night fell over Rysse, protestors clashed with SCSI forces and the forces of the principate, however, as the first 500 NDF troops began to fill the streets, the protestors quickly dispersed, in the meantime Malben had flown into Rysse airport under heavy guard to meet in the terminal with the Council of Angmaar to order the declaration of martial law in Angmaar, vehemently condemning the violence the protestors had wrought.

By the morning of the 4th, the council had confirmed the death of the Prince of Angmaar to the government and citizens.
